newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed Martin backlog at end-Q2 $48.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin backlog at end-Q2 $48.1 bln.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp said Tuesday its backlog totalled $48.1 billion at the end of the second quarter of 1997, down from $50.9 billion at the end of the quarter a year ago.
The diversified aeronautics company said approximately half of the decline in the backlog could be attributed to divestitures made during the past three quarters.
It said those divestitures also affected sales for the second quarter, which totalled $6.9 billion, 3.0 percent lower than the $7.1 billion posted for the same quarter in 1996, it said.
Net earnings per share on a fully diluted basis for the latest quarter were $308 million or $1.40 a share compared with $299 million oir $1.33 a share for the year-ago quareter, it said.
"Our strong performance and caputure rate on new business continue to validate our consolidation strategy," said Norman Augustine, chairman and chief executive officer.

Augustine added that Lockheed Martin's proposed merger with Northrop Grumman NOC.N amnnounced earlier this month will even furtherenhance the company's competititveness and cost efficiency while furhter augmenting its growth prospects.
